## Eight common assumptions, negated

| # | Usual assumption | If it were false, what conditional effect would follow |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | A skip on edge 3 (node0→node3) is a roughly constant residual benefit. | Its value depends on the long path. It helps when that path is deep conv, and hurts when the path is weak and edge 3 must supply conv capacity itself. |
| A2 | Pooling effects add up and are mild regularisers wherever they sit. | Pooling stacked in series or in parallel over-smooths. A conv placed after or beside pooling then gains much more. |
| A3 | Parallel edges into a node act independently. | They substitute for or complement each other. Conv3x3 gains more beside a 1x1 or pool sibling and less beside a conv3x3 sibling. |
| A4 | The cost of removing an edge depends only on reachability. | The cost depends on whether the lost depth or capacity is supplied elsewhere, for example by a conv on edge 3 or edge 5. |
| A5 | More identity routes are always harmless. | Redundant identity routes into node 3 dilute the conv signal. A second skip then hurts. |
| A6 | Pooling right after a conv costs the same as pooling anywhere. | Pooling after a conv is a cheap regulariser. It costs less, or even helps, when the upstream edge is conv3x3. |
| A7 | The op on edge 0 matters little once later edges carry conv. | Edge 0 sets the depth of every path through node 1. A skip on edge 0 hurts more when later edges are shallow 1x1. |
| A8 | Conv gains are about the same everywhere in the cell. | Conv gains saturate. Adding conv3x3 where conv3x3 already exists elsewhere (edge 3) gives less. |

All 20 hypotheses below follow the constraints:
- Each one links two different edges.
- No condition makes the edited edge inert. For example, none conditions on edge 0 = none when edge 2 or edge 4 is edited, and none conditions on edge 5 = none when edge 1 or edge 2 is edited.
- No condition setting is used more than twice.
